title: Simplified Technical English review
redactions: Public export. Contains project messages and tool event metadata. Private paths, account metadata, hidden reasoning, attachments, and raw tool inputs and outputs are omitted or redacted.

text: Sprawdzę angielski w `INTENT.md` według skilla `asd-ste100` i przejrzę sformułowania, których linter nie ocenia.

The skill’s linter found **0 violations in 2,237 words**. I also reviewed the requirements and acceptance checks in strict mode and spot-checked general vocabulary against the Issue 9 dictionary.

Remaining edits with the clearest benefit:

| Line | Suggested wording |
| --- | --- |
| 13 | “Do not let two customer records have the same email address.” |
| 79 | Replace “with a valid status value” with “with one of the three status values.” |
| 89 | “Is it necessary for staff to keep document files in this version?” |
| 100 | “Do not do a checksum check.” |
| 131–133 | Use “Make sure that…” for each expected response. For example, “Make sure that the new document has status `PENDING`.” |
| 132 | “Set the planned handover date to null.” This identifies the input and avoids “clear” as a general verb. |
| 142 | Split the test setup into two sentences. “The dealership registers the vehicle. A `REGISTRATION_POA` document has status `VERIFIED` and no expiry date.” |
| 146 | Use `missingDocumentTypes` and `problems` consistently in the expected results. This removes ambiguity about which API fields to check. |

The independent review covered the skill’s structural checks and selected dictionary entries. It does not establish full word-by-word dictionary conformance. Fixed API identifiers and necessary dealership and software terms should stay. No files edited.
